review.notes: Chain starts at lineage v1 (DR2-EN084, 2005-10-20), the GOAT entry's exact text. The rest of the lineage is cosmetic and is not recorded: v0 (IOC-083, 2004-03-01) -> v1 is 'Send ... to destroy' -> 'By sending ..., destroy'; v2 (LCYW-EN249, 2012-09-29) is the PSCT rewrite where 'except this card' becomes 'destroy all other cards on the field' and '1 face-up "Umi" you control' codifies a requirement both scripts already enforce (cfilter/descostfilter both test IsFaceup and IsCode(CARD_UMI) on your side only); v3 (SBAD-EN025, 2019-05-30) is the GY rewording and is the pinned cdb text. The remaining script differences are non-behavioural: the operation-info recipient parameter (tp vs 0) and aux.TRUE vs a nil filter. No source in the packet dates the face-down self-destruction ruling, so effective is left empty rather than guessed.

event.historical_text: By sending "Umi" on your side of the field to the Graveyard, destroy all cards on the field except this card.
event.summary: Period ruling with no text counterpart: the GOAT script excludes Daedalus from its own mass destruction only while it is face-up ('e:GetHandler():IsFaceup() and e:GetHandler() or nil' in the exclusion argument of the operation's GetMatchingGroup), so a Daedalus turned face-down after the Ignition effect was activated is destroyed along with everything else. The modern script excludes it whenever it is still related to the effect ('local exc=c:IsRelateToEffect(e) and c or nil'). Upstream's own note on the variant: 'If the card is facedown, it's sent as well.' Cost and activation legality are the same in both: a face-up 'Umi' you control, sendable as cost, with at least one other card on either field.
